name: Sternwarte und Planetarium Innsbruck
beschreibung:
### Overview
The Historical Observatory of the University of Innsbruck lies in the north-east of the Botanical Garden in the Hötting district. It was built in 1904 by astronomer Egon von Oppolzer to his own plans and with private funds, and in 1909 it was attached to the University as its observatory. Today the well-preserved site, with its original instruments – including a 40 cm Zeiss mirror telescope – is an important monument to Austrian scientific history. Since 2014 it has been open to visitors as the Museum Historische Sternwarte; part of the collection can also be explored via a 360-degree multimedia tour.

### Route & Requirements
The observatory can be visited on guided tours; the museum is regularly open on Thursdays from 3.30 to 5.30 pm. A tour takes in the historic rooms and the observation dome with its original instruments. No prior knowledge is needed and there are no particular physical demands. Suitable for children and adults alike. As the site includes outdoor areas and unheated historic rooms, weatherproof clothing is recommended.

### Getting There
The observatory is located at Sternwartestraße 13 and can also be reached via the main entrance of the Botanical Garden at Botanikerstraße 10. From Innsbruck Central Station, IVB public transport takes you to the Hötting/Botanical Garden area. Drivers reach Innsbruck via the A12 Inntal motorway (Innsbruck West exit) and follow signs towards Hötting. Parking is available in the surrounding streets; arriving by public transport is recommended.

### Tips
If possible, visit on a Thursday afternoon and combine it with a stroll through the Botanical Garden with its alpine and display greenhouses. If you cannot be there in person, try the University's 360-degree multimedia tour. For observing the night sky through a telescope, the Institute of Astro- and Particle Physics also offers the Astronacht (astronomy night) in the winter semester, with advance registration.
